questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Volume of a Parallelepiped Spanned by Three Position Vectors Given Their Coordinates
questions.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(2,1,2)$, $B(3,3,3)$, $C(-2,-1,3)$, and $D(4,1,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(3i+3j+3k)-(2i+j+2k) \\  & =i+2j+k \\  & =⟨1,2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2i-j+3k)-(2i+j+2k) \\  & =-4i-2j+k \\  & =⟨-4,-2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(4i+j+4k)-(2i+j+2k) \\  & =2i+2k \\  & =⟨2,0,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =((-2)\cdot 2-0\cdot 1)-2((-4)\cdot 2-2\cdot 1)+((-4)\cdot 0-2\cdot (-2)) \\  & =-4+20+4 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|20|=20.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar
questions.problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,1,t⟩$, $q=⟨2,-1,-1⟩$, and $r=⟨3,0,1⟩$ are coplanar.
questions.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}t & 1 & t \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+t\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =t((-1)\cdot 1-0\cdot (-1))-(2\cdot 1-3\cdot (-1))+t(2\cdot 0-3\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-t-5+3t \\  & =2t-5.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 2t-5 & =0 \\ 2t & =5 \\ t & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=\frac{5}{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar
questions.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨8,4,6⟩,$ $b=⟨8,-4,5⟩,$ and $c=⟨0,2,k⟩$ are coplanar.
questions.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & 6 \\ 8 & -4 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =8\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 5 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}|+6\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =8(-4\cdot k-2\cdot 5)-4(8\cdot k-0\cdot 5)+6(8\cdot 2-0\cdot (-4)) \\  & =-32k-80-32k+96 \\  & =16-64k \\  & =16(1-4k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 16(1-4k) & =0 \\ 1-4k & =0 \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=\frac{1}{4}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Volume of a Parallelepiped Spanned by Three Position Vectors Given Their Coordinates
questions.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(3,0,1),$ $B(0,-1,3),$ $C(1,-2,2),$ and $D(2,2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-j+3k)-(3i+k) \\  & =-3i-j+2k \\  & =⟨-3,-1,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i-2j+2k)-(3i+k) \\  & =-2i-2j+k \\  & =⟨-2,-2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(2i+2j+k)-(3i+k) \\  & =-i+2j \\  & =⟨-1,2,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3((-2)\cdot 0-2\cdot 1)+((-2)\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 1)+2((-2)\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2)) \\  & =6+1-12 \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-5|=5.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar
questions.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $x=⟨{k}^{2},-2,5⟩$, $y=⟨1,3,4⟩$, and $z=⟨0,-1,2⟩$ are coplanar.

**In ascending order:** $\,$

$k=${{field-1}}
$\,$
and
$\,$
$k=${{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}{k}^{2} & -2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & ={k}^{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|-(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & ={k}^{2}(3\cdot 2-4\cdot (-1))+2(1\cdot 2-4\cdot 0)+5(1\cdot -1-3\cdot 0) \\  & ={k}^{2}(6+4)+2(2)+5(-1) \\  & =10{k}^{2}+4-5 \\  & =10{k}^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =0 \\ 10{k}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ 10{k}^{2} & =1 \\ {k}^{2} & =\frac{1}{10} \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if 
$k=-\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}$ or $k=\sqrt{\frac{1}{10}}.$
